chapter: Childhood in Oklahoma, Kansas City and Tulsa
title: Schoolmates who became bass players
summary: Rufus, Charles Hadnott, Robert Lewis, Commodore Clark and Thurber Daisy, who left Tulsa to play bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: William Jett. Then there was a orchestra leader at school named Charles Grimm. And I asked him to let me play bass for him, because one boy had graduated from his class, named Rufus -- I can't remember Rufus' last name. He played bass and trombone. He went to Kansas City. And Charles Hadnott-- William Hadnott, what am I saying, Charles Hadnott the bass player that's out here now? He went to Kansas City, he didn't even finish school. He dropped out to go to Kansas City to play bass.
Then there was another boy, named Robert Lewis who came out here. He was later known to be called Baby Boy. He
worked with Lorenzo Flournoy's trio for a long while.

The next one to leave was a kid named Commodore Clark. And he was younger than I was, but he had been hanging around the orchestra room and picked up some pointers on his own, you know. He felt as though he could do it. So he left town. He dropped out at an early age.

And going back to this boy's uncle's hotel, I told you, it used to be? He turned out to be a bass player. His name was Thurber Daisy. He worked with Louis Jordan for a long while. Thurber. He was almost full Indian. He lives up here around Fresno now, houseful of kids.
